name: Low-profile spherical parallel 3-RRR wrapped around the shoulder
verdict: dead: gap 193.44 vs 68.93 for the 3R on the same bench; not worth a GPU sweep - the limiter is structural (leg closure / leg-leg collisions over the shoulder workspace, and nine rigid parts each clearing the highest skin they sweep)
limiter: kinematic workspace vs collisions: with every hub axis on reachable skin, the best closes 0.92 of poses but then loses 116-190/220 to leg-leg and leg-platform collisions; local short legs (entry 46) lose 97/220 to leg closure (leg 1: 56). Proximity: middle hubs 62-201 mm and links up to 204 mm from GH over skin 45-70 mm away (inband14 0.355)
note: best = sweep entry 46 (hub-axis accessibility enforced; entries 0-43 were measured without it and the best of those, 216.55, put middle hubs 300-400 mm from GH); bench fast Bench(60,160); 51 bench entries after ~2500 kinematic / quick-screen configurations; red team: rest - hub HW2 8.3 mm inside (q 0.95), Raise overhead 150 - P0 collides with the platform, workspace overhead 165 - leg 2 open, across-body plane 145 - leg 1 open, behind-back taken at 1.7 mm; baseline 3R 68.93
audit: audit 2026-10-15: death stands. Entry 46 re-measured on Bench(60,160) fast: identical (193.44). Upper bound with every adjacent-member collision waived: entry 46 187.80, entry 49 166.49 (reach 0.41, follow 0.75, inband14 0.049) - still ~100 above the 3R. Limiter: the 3 middle hubs sweep the shoulder and are fitted 150-400 mm from GH, so inband14 stays <= 0.36 whatever the collision rules.

mechanism.notes: Agile-Eye-type spherical 3-RRR. bodies: 3 proximal arc links, 3 distal arc links, platform ring + arm end (fixed to the arm). joints: 3 ACTIVE base hubs + 3 x 2 PASSIVE hubs (HW_i, HV_i), 9 O20 hubs; 2 loops (three legs). Passives set by the closures (spherical Grubler 3 (8 - 1 - 9) + 9 = 3): not sensed (the 3 base angles fix the platform). custom: base frame (3 hub seats + 2 straps), 6 links, platform (2 straps + arm end), 9 hub shafts (est.); catalogue: 9 x MR117 pair (est.).
